elsa-wels-tbilisi-2027.about:
Winter ELSA Law Schools (WELS) are one-week academic and cultural programmes run by local groups of the European Law Students' Association. WELS Tbilisi 2027 (21-28 Feb 2027) focuses on International Migration and Refugee Law, with lectures and workshops delivered with Academician Levan Alexidze Foundation. The academic level is intermediate, and the group is capped at 30 participants from across Europe and beyond.

Alongside the academic programme there is a social and cultural programme (city tours, themed nights and an optional Gala Ball). ELSA Law Schools are open to everyone: you do not need to be an ELSA member, a law student or even 18 to apply, though members pay a reduced fee. Hosted in Georgia, it is especially convenient for students from the South Caucasus.

You can apply to up to three Winter ELSA Law Schools in one application; the deadline is 22 November 2026, 23:59 CET.
highlights: Academic programme on International Migration and Refugee Law with Academician Levan Alexidze Foundation
International group of up to 30 participants
Accommodation, academic and social programme included in the fee
elsa-wels-tbilisi-2027.eligibility: Open to everyone (law students, young lawyers and other interested people; no age or nationality restriction stated). ELSA members pay lower fees; working language English.
how_to_apply: Open the Winter ELSA Law Schools portfolio and choose up to three schools
Fill in the unified WELS application form (motivation and preferences)
Submit before 22 November 2026, 23:59 CET
If selected, confirm and pay the participation fee
elsa-wels-tbilisi-2027.costs: Participation fee covers accommodation, academic and social programme: EUR 335 (ELSA member, favoured country), EUR 375 (ELSA member, non-favoured country), up to EUR 460 for non-members. Optional extras (Gala Ball about EUR 50-55, airport transfer EUR 30). Travel not included.

algoma-university-international-entrance.about:
Algoma University in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario (with campuses in Brampton and Timmins), offers merit scholarships to international secondary-school graduates entering a first undergraduate degree. The Chancellor's Award is CA$5,000 a year (CA$20,000 renewable) for an A+ average or equivalent (90–100% for internationals studying in Ontario); the President's Award (CA$2,500) and Dean's Award (CA$1,000) are one-time entrance awards for slightly lower averages.

Scholarships apply only to undergraduate degrees, and missed award deadlines lead to revocation. Algoma notes that entrance and renewal scholarships are under review for 2027–28, so confirm amounts before you apply.
highlights: CA$20,000 renewable Chancellor's Award
Entrance awards from CA$1,000
Undergraduate degrees only
algoma-university-international-entrance.eligibility: International secondary-school graduates entering year 1 of an Algoma undergraduate degree with strong averages and English requirements met. All nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to Algoma
Submit official results (IGCSE/A-level/IB or national)
Check the award deadlines on the Scholarships page
Keep renewal requirements

central-arkansas-international-student-m.about:
The University of Central Arkansas in Conway, a mid-sized public university with relatively low costs, runs an International Student Merit Scholarship for eligible first-time degree-seeking international students: $4,000 per semester, up to $32,000 over four years. Eligibility requirements and application details are linked from UCA's international scholarships page.

UCA also has scholarships for continuing international students based on achievement, leadership and campus involvement.
highlights: $4,000 per semester
Up to $32,000 over four years
Affordable public university
central-arkansas-international-student-m.eligibility: First-time degree-seeking international students meeting UCA's merit criteria. All nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Apply to UCA as an international first-year
Check the merit scholarship eligibility and application details
Submit any scholarship form required

gothenburg-axel-adler-scholarship-2027.about:
The Axel Adler Scholarship is a tuition fee waiver for students who must pay tuition in Sweden and have applied to an international bachelor's or master's programme at the University of Gothenburg as their first priority. One scholarship is awarded per master's programme and per eligible bachelor's programme (four across the Artistic Faculty), with up to ten extra for the most-applied programmes; selection is mainly based on your qualifications for the programme. A separate Axel Adler Scholarship for Sustainability supports sustainability-focused master's programmes.

Apply at universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027 and pay the fee and upload documents by 1 February 2027. Eligible applicants receive an email with scholarship instructions around 10 February; results come on 12 April (master's) and 15 April (bachelor's) 2027.
highlights: Full tuition waiver
Bachelor's and master's
Programme deadline 15 Jan 2027
gothenburg-axel-adler-scholarship-2027.eligibility: Fee-paying (non-EU/EEA) applicants who list a Gothenburg international programme first and meet entry requirements. Georgia and Qatar citizens may apply.
how_to_apply: Apply at universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027 with Gothenburg first
Pay the fee and upload documents by 1 February 2027
Follow the emailed scholarship instructions (~10 Feb 2027)
Results 12/15 April 2027
gothenburg-axel-adler-scholarship-2027.costs: Tuition fee waiver for the programme; living costs not covered.

iowa-nonresident-international-merit-sch.about:
The University of Iowa in Iowa City, a Big Ten research university known for writing, health sciences and engineering, considers all admitted first-years entering fall 2027 for merit scholarships, with or without test scores. Its non-resident awards (shown on the international scholarships page) are worth $2,000–15,000 a year for up to four years; if you qualify for several, you receive the highest.

Submit a complete application by 1 February 2027 and any test scores from tests taken through 12 December 2026; scores sent by 8 February 2027 can earn additional awards. Iowa recalculates all GPAs for consistency.
highlights: Test-optional consideration
Complete application by 1 Feb 2027
iowa-nonresident-international-merit-sch.eligibility: Admitted non-resident (including international) first-year students for fall 2027. All nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Apply to Iowa by 1 February 2027
Send SAT/ACT taken by 12 Dec 2026 (optional)
Self-report new scores by 8 Feb 2027 for extra awards
iowa-nonresident-international-merit-sch.costs: $2,000–15,000 per year for up to four years.

memorial-university-international-entran.about:
Memorial University of Newfoundland in St. John's, one of Canada's more affordable universities for international students, considers admitted internationals automatically for its entrance scholarships: the Memorial University International Entrance Scholarship, the IUGS Entrance Scholarship, the Fortis Inc. – H. Stanley Marshall Scholarship, the Killam American Undergraduate Scholarship (US students), the Don and Mona Dooley (OLOF) Thailand Scholarship, the Shona Perry-Maidment Entrance Award and the Convera Scholarship.

Awards cover first year only, are non-renewable and depend on available funding; transfer students qualify only if transferring fewer than 31 credit hours.
highlights: Seven international entrance awards
Automatic consideration
Low tuition by Canadian standards
memorial-university-international-entran.eligibility: International students admitted to a first undergraduate degree at Memorial (some awards country-specific). All nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Apply to Memorial
Meet admission requirements
Awards are assessed automatically
memorial-university-international-entran.costs: Values vary by award; first year only.

unr-international-student-scholarships-2.about:
The University of Nevada, Reno, a public research university with international tuition of about $23,500 a year, offers scholarships to international students: $1,000–12,000 for new international students and general university scholarships of $500–8,000 a year, plus department awards.

To be considered for many university and department scholarships you complete the annual scholarship application in MyNEVADA, which opens on 1 October; priority goes to applications completed by 1 February (final deadline mid-February to May depending on the office).
highlights: $1,000–12,000 for new internationals
Low international tuition (~$23,500)
Priority scholarship deadline 1 Feb 2027
unr-international-student-scholarships-2.eligibility: New international undergraduate students admitted to UNR. All nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Apply to UNR as an international student
Complete the scholarship application in MyNEVADA (opens 1 Oct 2026)
Submit by 1 February 2027 for priority

uottawa-differential-tuition-fee-exempti.about:
The University of Ottawa, the world's largest bilingual (English–French) university, offers the Differential Tuition Fee Exemption Scholarship to international students enrolled in French-taught programmes (including French immersion streams). It removes the international 'differential' part of tuition, so recipients pay fees close to the Canadian rate, which can save tens of thousands of dollars a year.

Students in English-taught programmes are instead considered for the International English Admission and Academic Excellence scholarships (up to CA$70,000). Check the uOttawa page for language requirements and renewal conditions.
highlights: Pay roughly domestic fees
For French-taught or immersion programmes
Renewable with good standing
uottawa-differential-tuition-fee-exempti.eligibility: International students admitted to French-taught (or immersion) undergraduate programmes at uOttawa who meet French-language requirements. All nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Choose a French-taught or French immersion programme
Apply to uOttawa and meet French-language requirements
Exemption is applied with admission if eligible
Keep renewal conditions

upei-international-entrance-awards-2027.about:
The University of Prince Edward Island in Charlottetown grants entrance awards each year to international students joining from high schools in Canada or abroad. Awards range from CA$1,000 to CA$3,000, credited to your student account, for converted averages of 90–100% and/or a top 5–10% class ranking.

You are considered automatically when your application is evaluated, but funds are limited, so early applications are strongly encouraged. After first year, students can compete for UPEI's academic excellence awards.
highlights: CA$1,000–3,000 entrance award
Automatic when admitted
Apply early: limited funds
upei-international-entrance-awards-2027.eligibility: International students entering UPEI from secondary school with 90%+ averages or top 5–10% rank. All nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Apply to UPEI early
Submit transcripts showing average/class rank
Award is decided with your admission letter

utah-international-freshman-merit-schola.about:
The University of Utah in Salt Lake City, a major public research university, awards merit scholarships to incoming freshmen based on unweighted high-school GPA, renewable for up to four years: President John R. Park Scholarship $10,000 (4.00 GPA), Provost's $8,000 (3.90), Bonneville $6,000 (3.80), and further awards of $4,000 and $3,000 for slightly lower GPAs. The scholarships are listed on Utah's international admissions pages.

The merit scholarship deadline is 1 December: by then you must submit the Common Application, pay the fee (or have a waiver) and ask your school to send official transcripts.
highlights: $3,000–10,000 a year by GPA
Renewable for four years
Deadline 1 Dec 2026
utah-international-freshman-merit-schola.eligibility: International first-year applicants entering in summer/fall 2027. All nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Submit the Common Application to Utah by 1 December 2026
Pay the fee or obtain a waiver
Request official transcripts be sent by 1 Dec (checked by 7 Dec)
utah-international-freshman-merit-schola.costs: $3,000–10,000 per year for up to four years.

aalto-asci-international-summer-research.about:
The Aalto University Science Institute (AScI) International Summer Research Programme hires 50+ research-driven students each summer to work as research assistants in groups across Aalto's School of Science and its three Schools of Engineering in Espoo, near Helsinki. Projects range from physics, mathematics and computer science to materials, energy and neuroscience; students apply to one to three projects from a list published in mid-December. In 2026 there were 5,500 applications from 133 countries and 70 interns from 28 countries.

The internship lasts 12 weeks in June–August (flexible by group) and includes a 'get to know Finland' course and a poster exhibition. Interns are employed by the research group with a salary of 2,000+ EUR per month depending on years of study, a travel bonus of 400 EUR (from inside Europe) or 800 EUR (from outside Europe), paid time off and help finding low-cost student housing.
highlights: Salaried research job in a top Nordic university (2,000+ EUR/month)
Travel bonus up to 800 EUR for students from outside Europe
Open worldwide; choose up to three projects
aalto-asci-international-summer-research.eligibility: Bachelor's and master's students worldwide (doctoral students only in exceptional cases) with a strong research interest. No nationality restriction.
how_to_apply: Read the programme pages and FAQ; the project list is published about 10 December 2026
Pick one to three projects
Combine the motivation letter, CV, transcripts and other compulsory attachments into one PDF in the required order
Ask a referee to email the recommendation letter directly to AScI by the deadline
Submit the online form between 7 and 31 January 2027 (23:59 UTC+2)
aalto-asci-international-summer-research.costs: No fees. Salary 2,000+ EUR per month (depends on years of study), travel bonus 400/800 EUR (inside/outside Europe), paid time off; interns pay their own rent (help finding student housing).

academia-sinica-taiwan-international-int.about:
The Taiwan International Internship Program (TIIP) is run by Academia Sinica, Taiwan's leading research institution, linked to its Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP). Interns spend the summer in an Academia Sinica lab in Taipei working with a host mentor across life sciences, physical sciences, computing and more.

It is designed to introduce strong international students to research in Taiwan and to recruit them into TIGP PhD programmes. The 2027 host mentors are already listed on the site, and the application portal is linked from the Apply page.

The programme offers financial support (detailed on its 'Financial and Other Supports' page).
highlights: Summer research in Taiwan's top research institute
2027 host mentors already listed
Financial support provided; pathway to TIGP PhD
academia-sinica-taiwan-international-int.eligibility: Third-year and final-year undergraduates, master's students, and holders of a BS or master's degree. Not eligible: PhD students, previous TIIP participants, and current Academia Sinica staff.
how_to_apply: Read the eligibility and timeline pages on tiip.dia.sinica.edu.tw.
Browse the 2027 host mentor list and choose mentors.
Apply through the online portal linked from the Apply page.
Contact tiip@as.edu.tw with questions.
academia-sinica-taiwan-international-int.costs: Financial support is provided; see the official Financial and Other Supports page for amounts.

australian-mathematics-competition-2027.about:
The Australian Mathematics Competition (AMC), run by the Australian Mathematics Trust since 1978, is a problem-solving contest taken by hundreds of thousands of students. The 2027 competition is sat at school between Tuesday 3 and Thursday 5 August 2027, on paper or online.

Divisions: Middle Primary (Years 3–4), Upper Primary (5–6), Junior (7–8), Intermediate (9–10) and Senior (11–12), plus a new Early Primary division for Years 1–2 from 2027. International schools can enter, with an earlier deadline for printed papers sent abroad.

Every student gets a result and certificate; top scorers receive prizes and medals, and a strong AMC score is a useful early signal for national olympiad pathways.
highlights: Taken by students in dozens of countries
Paper or online, sat at your own school
Certificates for all, medals for top scorers
australian-mathematics-competition-2027.eligibility: School students in Years 1–12. Entry is through a registered school (in Australia, New Zealand or internationally); students cannot usually enter alone.
how_to_apply: Ask your school maths coordinator to register on the AMT admin portal (competitions.amt.edu.au/admin).
International printed entries must be registered by 25 June 2027; online entries by 30 July 2027.
Sit the paper at school between 3 and 5 August 2027.
Results and certificates are released by AMT after marking.
australian-mathematics-competition-2027.costs: AUD 9.30 per student (bundle discounts available); paid by the school.

china-international-college-students-inn.about:
The China International College Students' Innovation Competition (CICSIC) is organised by China's Ministry of Education and partners. Its Higher Education Main Track ranks international entries separately from Chinese ones, by level (undergraduate or postgraduate) and stage (idea or registered startup).

In 2026 international registration ran 20 August – 15 September, followed by eligibility review, online evaluation from late September to October, and an on-site grand final in Nanjing in November (online presentation possible). International projects competed for 60 gold, 120 silver and 420 bronze awards. The 2027 edition is expected to follow the same calendar.

It is free to enter and a strong line on a CV for student entrepreneurs, with networking with Chinese investors and universities.
highlights: 600 awards reserved for international teams
Idea-stage projects welcome
Free entry; finals in China with online option
china-international-college-students-inn.eligibility: Teams of 2–15 students currently enrolled at (or graduated after 2021 from) a single non-Chinese higher-education institution; team leader under 35. Idea-stage (no company) or startup-stage (registered company, leader is legal representative). Materials in English or Chinese.
how_to_apply: Watch cy.ncss.cn/en for the 2027 invitation notice (expected August 2027).
Register the team on the PILC platform (pilcchina.org) during the registration window.
Upload a business plan PDF (optional one-minute video) and proof of student status.
Pass eligibility review and online evaluation; finalists are invited to the grand final.
china-international-college-students-inn.costs: Free to enter. Finalists' travel arrangements are announced in the notice; online presentation is possible.

cira-kyoto-research-internship-2027.about:
CiRA is Kyoto University's centre for induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cell research. Its Research Internship Program lets students spend 1–6 consecutive weeks in a host lab between June and October, joining lab work, doing basic experiments and presenting their results at the end.

It is aimed mainly at third- and fourth-year undergraduates and graduate students who may later join CiRA as graduate students or postdocs. Each lab takes at most one overseas student, so places are few and competitive.

CiRA covers a round trip to Kyoto (partly) and accommodation up to JPY 5,500 per day. Overseas students pay a short-term student fee (JPY 29,700/month in 2026) unless their university has an exchange agreement with Kyoto University.
highlights: Lab placement at a world-leading stem-cell institute
Partial travel and accommodation support
Pathway to graduate study at Kyoto University
cira-kyoto-research-internship-2027.eligibility: Undergraduates (mainly 3rd–4th year) and graduate students at overseas universities, planning to start graduate school within one or two years. Any nationality. English is the working language in most labs.
how_to_apply: Read the internship page and the list of host PIs; email a host PI before applying (recommended).
Fill in the application form and written pledge, and get consent from your home supervisor.
Submit by the overseas deadline (early February).
Results are announced around the end of March.
Arrange personal accident and liability insurance before arrival.
cira-kyoto-research-internship-2027.costs: Round trip and accommodation (up to JPY 5,500/day) partly covered. Short-term student fee of JPY 29,700/month for overseas students (waived for Kyoto University partner institutions). No stipend.

elsa-wels-antalya-2027.about:
Winter ELSA Law Schools (WELS) are one-week academic and cultural programmes run by local groups of the European Law Students' Association. WELS Antalya 2027 (31 Jan - 7 Feb 2027) focuses on Competition and Corporate Law, with lectures and workshops delivered with Antalya Bar Association and Akdeniz University. The academic level is intermediate, and the group is capped at 40 participants from across Europe and beyond.

Alongside the academic programme there is a social and cultural programme (city tours, themed nights and an optional Gala Ball). ELSA Law Schools are open to everyone: you do not need to be an ELSA member, a law student or even 18 to apply, though members pay a reduced fee.

You can apply to up to three Winter ELSA Law Schools in one application; the deadline is 22 November 2026, 23:59 CET.

International group of up to 40 participants
Accommodation, academic and social programme included in the fee
elsa-wels-antalya-2027.eligibility: Open to everyone (law students, young lawyers and other interested people; no age or nationality restriction stated). ELSA members pay lower fees; working language English.
how_to_apply: Open the Winter ELSA Law Schools portfolio and choose up to three schools
Fill in the unified WELS application form (motivation and preferences)
Submit before 22 November 2026, 23:59 CET
If selected, confirm and pay the participation fee
elsa-wels-antalya-2027.costs: Participation fee covers accommodation, academic and social programme: EUR 365 (ELSA member, favoured country), EUR 405 (ELSA member, non-favoured country), up to EUR 460 for non-members. Optional extras (Gala Ball about EUR 50-55, airport transfer EUR 30). Travel not included.

estiem-circular-economy-course-groningen.about:
Hosted by ESTIEM Local Group Groningen, this is the third edition of the Circular Economy Course, "Circular Economy: Innovate, Regenerate, Thrive" (7-12 December 2026). Through workshops, case studies and company input it explains how to move from the take-make-dispose model to systems where products are reused, repaired and recycled, cutting waste and emissions and building economic resilience.

The course takes 15 participants; ESTIEM events are week-long, student-run and all-inclusive for a small fee (EUR 105). Apply by 7 November 2026.

The 18th edition (Madrid, 27-29 November 2026) looks at sustainable fashion: what leading brands are doing, next-generation textiles and supply-chain changes to reduce waste, circular, resale and rental business models, and practical steps for a sustainable wardrobe.

Unusually for ESTIEM, this edition is open to students, alumni, professors and friends, and places are given first come, first served (15 places). Fee EUR 100 for students.

ESTIEM's Lean Six Sigma (LSS) courses teach the principles of Lean and Six Sigma - eliminating waste and reducing variability in business processes - through training sessions, case studies and an exam. The Central Course takes place in Dresden from 5 to 11 January 2027 for up to 20 participants. Applications run 1-20 November 2026; fee EUR 120, all-inclusive.

global-young-scientists-summit-2027.about:
The Global Young Scientists Summit (GYSS), organised by Singapore's National Research Foundation, brings together young scientists and leading minds from around the world under the theme 'Transcending Borders'. The 2027 summit takes place from 4 to 8 January 2027 in Singapore.

The format includes plenary lectures, panel huddles, quickfire pitches, fireside chats and site visits to Singapore research institutes, with close interaction with Nobel laureates, Fields Medallists, Turing Award winners and other eminent scientists.

Participants (mainly PhD students and early postdocs in science, technology, engineering, mathematics and medicine) attend through nomination by GYSS partner universities and research institutions worldwide.

habitat-global-village-siem-reap-cambodi.about:
Global Village is Habitat for Humanity's short-term volunteer travel programme. On this trip (7–13 November 2027) a team of international volunteers works alongside a local family, a building contractor and community volunteers. Volunteers help with mixing concrete and mortar, erecting walls and digging and pouring foundations; the drive to the site can take up to two hours a day, and the week ends with a home dedication.

The week typically runs: arrival, orientation and welcome dinner, four to five build days (with one cultural/social learning exchange activity), a farewell and home dedication, then departure. No construction experience is needed; work can be strenuous, so volunteers should be in good health.

The programme donation (US$1,860) covers shared hotel rooms, meals and in-country costs and supports the family's home; flights are extra. It is a meaningful volunteering experience for students and families and a good topic for university application essays.

Youth 15–17 welcome with a parent or authorised adult
Accommodation, meals and in-country logistics included

Pay the non-refundable deposit or start fundraising, then book flights.
habitat-global-village-siem-reap-cambodi.costs: Programme donation US$1,860 covering double-room hotel accommodation, meals (breakfast, build-site lunches, dinners) and in-country costs. International flights, insurance and visa are extra.

hku-chemistry-summer-research-programme-.about:
Run through the HKU Summer Institute, CHEM4990 places undergraduates from outside HKU in a Department of Chemistry research group for four weeks, preferably starting in late June or early July 2027 (exact dates agreed with the supervisor). It is non-credit-bearing and fully in person.

Applicants need at least one year of chemistry with a lab component, and must upload a CV and transcript; shortlisted candidates are interviewed. It is a good fit for chemistry students who want lab experience in Asia before applying for graduate school.

Applications open on a rolling basis from late November 2026: early-bird deadline 31 January 2027, non-local deadline 10 April 2027.

Electrosynthesis replaces toxic reagents with electric current and is one of the fastest-growing areas of green chemistry; the workshop is hands-on in HKU chemistry labs.

It is open to undergraduate and postgraduate students from local and non-local universities, and is best for chemistry and chemical engineering students. It is non-credit bearing with a certificate of attendance.

hku-from-curiosity-to-research-2027.about:

Sessions cover planning a research strategy from identifying needs to producing output, qualitative and quantitative methods, critical reading of statistical analysis and professional research writing, plus a 'Master Series' session, a capstone and a session on research postgraduate studies at HKU.

hku-from-curiosity-to-research-2027.costs: Programme fee in HKD to be announced (10% early-bird discount by 31 Jan 2027). Application fee HKD 400. Accommodation, visa (HKD 1,100) and travel extra.

iterative-winter-2027-batch.about:
Iterative is a Singapore-based accelerator and seed fund focused on founders building in Southeast Asia. Twice a year it runs a batch; the Winter 2027 batch runs from February to May 2027, beginning with a four-day in-person orientation, after which founders stay in their home market and work remotely with the partners.

It invests in all industries and stages, including startups that are only an idea, assessing market, evidence and founders. Student and recent-graduate founders building for Southeast Asian markets are eligible.

Each company receives US$150,000–500,000 for roughly 10–15%, paid in full on admission with no milestones, clawbacks or programme fees.
highlights: US$150k–500k invested upfront, no fees
Idea-stage startups can apply
Remote after a 4-day in-person orientation
iterative-winter-2027-batch.eligibility: Founders (any nationality) building startups for Southeast Asian markets. Only founders may attend interviews and batch events. No minimum traction required.
how_to_apply: Read the batch details on iterative.vc/apply.
Sign up for the deadline reminder and prepare a short written application about your market, evidence and team.
Submit the online application for the Winter 2027 batch.
Shortlisted founders are interviewed by the partners.
iterative-winter-2027-batch.costs: No programme fee. Investment of US$150k–500k for about 10–15% equity. Travel to the orientation at your own cost.

japan-youth-summit-2027.about:
The Japan Youth Summit is an annual international youth conference held in Japan (organiser address in Osaka) by the Youth Break the Boundaries (YBB) Foundation. The fifth edition, in 2027, asks young delegates to design innovative solutions that harmonise sustainability with the preservation of cultural heritage, aligned with SDGs 4, 9, 11, 12 and 13.

Delegates attend panels, workshops, group projects and cultural visits, and present their ideas. It is open to high school students, university students and young professionals worldwide.

Self-funded delegates are accepted without competitive selection (registration until 10 April 2027); fully funded delegates (programme fee covered) are chosen by essays, interview and evaluation (deadline 20 December 2026). Flights and visas are not covered.
highlights: Fully funded places cover the programme fee
Open to school and university students worldwide
Sustainability and cultural-heritage focus in Japan
japan-youth-summit-2027.eligibility: Young people of any nationality: high school students, university students and young professionals (see the guidebook for exact age limits). Programme in English.
how_to_apply: Read the English guideline PDF on japanyouthsummit.com.
Pick fully funded (essays + interview, by 20 Dec 2026) or self-funded (by 10 Apr 2027).
Register online and pay the registration fee (USD 10 fully funded / USD 15 self-funded).
Self-funded delegates pay the programme fee in batches; check visa requirements for Japan.
japan-youth-summit-2027.costs: Registration fee USD 10 (fully funded) or USD 15 (self-funded); self-funded delegates also pay a programme fee in instalments (see /fees). Fully funded: programme fee covered. Travel and visa extra.

jef-climate-and-democracy-conference-bru.about:
The Climate and Democracy Conference is the final event of JEF Europe's ClimDM (Climate and Democracy Mainstreaming) workplan. Over three days (3-5 December 2026) in Brussels, at the European Parliament (to be confirmed) and the JEF Europe office, participants discuss the crossroads of climate and democracy with policymakers, activists, civil society and politicians.

Participants contribute directly to JEF Europe's Climate and Democracy Manifesto and help present it to politicians, youth parties and climate NGOs. Travel is reimbursed up to EUR 200 and two nights' accommodation and meals are fully covered. The deadline is very close: 1 November 2026, 23:59 CET.
highlights: Travel up to EUR 200, accommodation and meals covered
Meet EU policymakers in Brussels
Co-write a youth Climate and Democracy Manifesto
jef-climate-and-democracy-conference-bru.eligibility: Young people interested in European politics and climate; JEF events are generally for ages 18-35. No nationality restriction stated on the call.
how_to_apply: Read the call on the JEF Europe website
Fill in the application form
Submit before 1 November 2026, 23:59 CET
jef-climate-and-democracy-conference-bru.costs: Free; travel reimbursed up to EUR 200; accommodation (2 nights) and meals covered.

keio-bio2q-research-internship-2027.about:
Bio2Q is a World Premier International Research Center (WPI) at Keio University that combines human biology, microbiome science and quantum computation. Its 2027 Research Internship Program hosts students in Bio2Q labs for 8–12 weeks between 10 May and 10 August 2027, with exact dates agreed with the host lab.

It targets students who are considering a master's or PhD at Keio: bachelor's and master's students for the Graduate School of Medicine, and master's students for Science and Technology or Pharmaceutical Sciences. Recent graduates may also apply, and English is the working language.

Bio2Q provides designated accommodation and travel expenses (subject to conditions). Selection is by document review and an online interview, with results around February 2027.
highlights: Housing and travel covered
English-only, no prior lab contact needed
Cutting-edge mix of microbiome, medicine and quantum computing
keio-bio2q-research-internship-2027.eligibility: Bachelor's and master's students (or recent graduates) worldwide aiming at Keio's Graduate School of Medicine; master's students aiming at a PhD in Science and Technology or Pharmaceutical Sciences. No Japanese or language certificate required if you communicate in English.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 guidelines PDF on the Bio2Q news page.
Choose up to three labs in the Keio Web Entry System and write one Statement of Purpose.
Submit documents online (or by email) by 1 December 2026, 23:59 JST.
Attend an online interview if shortlisted; final results around February 2027.
keio-bio2q-research-internship-2027.costs: Designated accommodation and travel expenses are provided (travel subject to conditions). No stipend or living allowance.
